as_told.title: Ning Li's superconductor weight loss results

plain: In the 1990s, a physicist named Ning Li at the University of Alabama in Huntsville studied whether superconductors, materials that carry electricity with no resistance, could make objects lighter. Michels tells this on two episodes. In one, he places her under a researcher named Larry Smalley. In the other, he says she published results with a colleague named Douglas Torr, showing the masses she tested lost between 0.5% and 2.1% of their weight over several trials. If it held up, it would be a step toward antigravity.
